references.text: An oath sworn to the Lord must be kept and not broken, which explains why the leaders felt bound by the oath they had sworn to the Gibeonites.
The Preacher warns that it is better not to make a vow than to make one and fail to keep it, highlighting the seriousness of the leaders' oath.
The earlier context in which Israel's leaders made a covenant and swore an oath to the Gibeonites without consulting the Lord.
David had to atone for Saul breaking this oath by killing Gibeonites, demonstrating the serious consequences of violating an oath sworn in the Lord's name.
Ezekiel describes how breaking an oath and a covenant leads to God's judgment, emphasizing the importance of keeping the oath even when it was made under deception.
The psalm describes the righteous person who keeps their oath even when it is to their own harm, reflecting the leaders' decision to honor the oath.
